title: Generating proteins with computationally predicted functions and multiple states via multimodal diffusion
desc: Jing et al. present ProDiT, a multimodal diffusion model that generates diverse, functionally conditioned proteins, including multistate proteins, expanding capabilities beyond existing generative protein design methods. Generating proteins with the full diversity and complexity of functions found in nature is a grand challenge in protein design. Here we present protein diffusion transformer (ProDiT), a multimodal diffusion model that unifies sequence and structure modelling paradigms to enable the generation of proteins with computationally predicted functions at scale. Trained on sequences, three-dimensional structures and annotations for 128 million proteins across the evolutionary landscape, ProDiT generates diverse, novel proteins that are computationally predicted to preserve known active- and binding-site motifs and can be conditioned on a wide range of molecular functions, spanning 463 Gene Ontology terms. We introduce a diffusion sampling protocol to design proteins with multiple functional states, and illustrate this protocol by computationally scaffolding enzymatic active sites from carbonic anhydrase and lysozyme such that they are predicted to be deactivated by a calcium effector. Our results showcase the capacity of ProDiT to satisfy design specifications inaccessible to existing generative models, thereby expanding the protein design toolkit.

title: Biometric Monitoring and Machine Learning to Improve Preoperative Risk Stratification in Major Non-cardiac Surgery
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre; conditions: Surgery, Postoperative Complications, Risk Assessment, Elective Surgical Procedure, Surgery-Complications; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 400; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Many patients undergoing surgery experience complications which can lead to reduced independence and quality of life. Prior to surgery, doctors attempt to anticipate the risk of complications using information about a patient's current health, lifestyle, and medical records. The more useful health information doctors have, the more accurately they can predict whether someone is likely to develop a complication. New technology, such as wearables (e.g., smartwatches), which are widely available and frequently used by the general public, can provide detailed health information outside of the immediate clinical environment, such as heart rate, steps taken/distance walked in a day, and sleep quality. The study is looking at whether the information from such a device could be used by doctors to more reliably predict who is likely to experience complications following surgery. The study will consist of two phases. The first phase (piloting) will examine practical difficulties in recruiting patients and having them wear the device. In the second phase, we will assess if the information provided by the wearable is indeed able to help predict which patients are most likely to develop complications after surgery. All participants in both phases of the study will be asked to wear the device for 48 hours in the 3 months before their scheduled surgery.

title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning
desc: Conventional artificial neurons separate spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, limiting their ability to model irregular observations. We introduce the Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neuron (DAWIN), a continuous-time primitive for replacing standard neural layers in MLPs, Transformers, and graph neural networks. DAWIN couples spatial projection with elapsed-time-dependent wave excitation and integrates it into a local complex state through closed-form damped evolution, avoiding numerical differential equation solvers. We show that DAWIN generalizes static sinusoidal and memoryless wave neurons on interval-augmented inputs, derive closed-form gradients, and establish bounded-input bounded-output stability for positive damping and sampling intervals bounded away from zero. An associative Triton prefix-scan implementation, DAWINLinear, uses FP32 accumulation and achieves O(log L) parallel depth for sequence length L. Across 11 parameter-matched tasks covering irregular oscillators, MuJoCo dynamics, pedestrian trajectories, and PhysioNet 2012 clinical sequences, DAWIN outperforms Neural CDE on 9 tasks and ReLU-MLP on 8. It achieves the lowest error on dense clinical dynamics (0.9531 NRMSE, winning across all 10 seeds) and ties for the best mortality prediction (0.9993 AUROC). Shuffling elapsed intervals increases error by 58.2%-77.4% on selected dynamics tasks, versus 0.06% on a time-irrelevant control, supporting reliance on physical timing. On NVIDIA B200 GPUs, parallel wave integration accelerates inference by up to 2,630 times over its serial implementation and reduces peak GPU memory by up to 97.6% relative to Mamba in the tested configurations.

title: MedDx, a training-free AI phenotyping model, identifies alcohol use disorder in cirrhosis with hepatologist-level agreement
desc: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is often under-documented in patients with cirrhosis, which delays treatment. Expert chart review of clinical notes can identify under-documented AUD, but is not scalable. We propose MedDx, an open-weight, training-free, and engine-agnostic language model, to phenotype AUD using clinical notes in patients with cirrhosis. We benchmarked MedDx on a 485-patient study cohort sampled from the 14,406-patient Indiana Cirrhosis Registry, using a chart-review-based reference as ground truth. MedDx agreed with the ground truth at three-class Cohen's {kappa} 0.92, against 0.67 for the AUD diagnosis code. It agreed with one hepatologist at 0.85 on all 485 charts and with a second at 0.82 on 186 charts, on which the two hepatologists agreed at 0.87. Weighted to the registry, its sensitivity was 98% and specificity 94%, against 63% and 96% for the AUD diagnosis code, and 61% of an estimated 6,223 patients with AUD had no AUD diagnosis by the first cirrhosis diagnosis. MedDx is openly available as an off-the-shelf, equitable, and auditable tool to identify AUD.

title: RecurSieve: A Python Package to Detect Subtle Gene Expression Differences Across Single-Cell RNA-seq Comparisons Using Iterative Machine Learning
desc: Most existing methods for performing differential expression testing using single-cell RNA-seq data evaluate genes independently and primarily detect shifts in mean RNA levels. These methods may thus miss RNAs that distinguish experimental groups jointly or through changes in the shape of genes' expression distributions. To address this limitation, we developed RecurSieve, an iterative ensemble learning method that combines shared expression classification with unsupervised clustering to recursively identify gene sets with group-based expression differences. Because experimental labels apply to heterogeneous populations of single cells within each comparative group, RecurSieve allows dynamic label reassignment during iterative training to detect subtle, non-linear expression patterns. In benchmarking experiments using simulated data with staged distributional expression differences, RecurSieve recovered more genes (2.3-3.9 of 10 staged genes) across groups as compared to standard methods (Wilcoxon, t-test, and logistic regression; 0.0-0.7 staged genes). When applied to a single nuclei RNA-seq analysis containing low and high-pathology stages of Alzheimer's disease (46 human donor brains), RecurSieve extended results from standard approaches by identifying genes including WWOX, DPP10, KCNIP4, HS6ST3, and CNTN5 which tend to exhibit stage-specific distributional expression differences accompanied by only minor changes in average expression. A subset of the genes exclusively detected in RecurSieve analysis had been previously associated with Alzheimer's disease, underscoring the potential importance resulting from the unique sensitivity of our method. These simulated and empirical single-cell RNA-seq results demonstrate how the RecurSieve framework complements standard methods for identifying genes with unique group-specific expression differences independent of changes in average expression.

title: Risk governance for generative AI mental health support: a multi-turn safety architecture
desc: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health support despite lacking mechanisms to safely govern evolving risk. Existing safety approaches primarily detect risk but rarely shape how models respond as conversational risk unfolds. We developed a portable, model-external safety governance architecture that combines contextual risk detection, reasoning-based verification, and protocol-guided response generation for multi-turn mental health interactions. Using synthetic conversations grounded in real-world mental health narratives, the architecture’s performance was assessed with GPT-5-chat and Qwen3.5-27B, increasing clinician-preferred escalation responses by 25.6–59.2 pp, while achieving high risk detection performance (specificity: 0.85 (95%CI: 0.78;0.91), sensitivity: 0.92 (95%CI: 0.89;0.95)). Performance remained stable across conversation length and across models (proprietary and open-source), with preliminary evidence showing that rapport and connection were preserved. These findings demonstrate that clinically-grounded governance can extend beyond risk detection to improve how LLMs manage evolving mental health risk, providing a framework for scalable safety governance.

title: Patient perceptions of artificial intelligence in breast disease management: a cross-sectional survey in China.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly integrated into healthcare, yet patient perceptions-particularly in breast disease management-remain underexplored. Understanding these attitudes is critical for optimizing AI implementation and addressing disparities in trust and acceptance. To assess patient attitudes toward AI tools in breast disease management and identify how age and education influence willingness to adopt AI in clinical settings in China. A cross-sectional, online, questionnaire-based survey was conducted among patients who underwent surgery for breast diseases in the Department of Breast Surgery at Peking Union Medical College Hospital (PUMCH) through the wenjuanxing application (a survey platform) from March to May 2025. Of 530 invited participants, 457 (response rate: 86.2%) completed the questionnaire, which evaluated prior AI use, trust levels, concerns, and willingness to engage with AI tools. Primary outcomes included perceptions of AI utility, trust in AI versus physician recommendations, privacy concerns, and willingness to use AI for pre-diagnosis, triage, and clinical decision support. Among participants, 91.7% found AI tools at least "somewhat helpful," though 66.7% cited lack of emotional support as a key drawback. When AI and physician advice conflicted, 50.8% fully trusted doctors, while 43.3% preferred integrating both. Willingness to use AI was high for pre-diagnosis (86.0%) and precise triage (92.1%), but lower for clinical diagnosis and treatment assistance (70.0%). Patients across different age groups and educational levels hold generally similar views on AI tools, yet distinct tendencies emerge among subgroups. Multivariable ordinal logistic regression revealed that patients aged over 45 tended to hold more negative evaluations of AI tools, whereas younger individuals showed more positive attitudes. Meanwhile, those with postgraduate education or above tended to express more negative attitudinal sentiment toward AI tools. Patients in this survey demonstrated strong acceptance of AI in breast disease management, but concerns about emotional support, privacy, and accuracy persist. Demographic variations highlight the need for tailored implementation strategies, including transparency protocols and equitable design. title: Artificial Intelligence-based CTV Segmentation in Breast Radiotherapy: Exploration of Large-scale Deployable Models, Including Intra- and Inter-center Probability Maps
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: IRCCS Ospedale San Raffaele; conditions: Breast Cancer; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 1500; status: ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING] The goal of this observational study is to evaluate artificial intelligence (AI) models that automatically outline the target area for radiotherapy, called the clinical target volume (CTV), in adult women treated with whole-breast radiotherapy for breast cancer. Outlining this area by hand is time-consuming and can differ between doctors and between hospitals. The main questions it aims to answer are: 1. How closely do AI-generated outlines agree with outlines approved by doctors, including in patients from hospitals not used to build the models? 2. How much do outlines vary within and between hospitals, and can AI help quantify and reduce this variability? 3. Which methods work best to build probability maps, which show for each point of the image how likely it is to belong to the target area? Researchers will use planning CT images and target outlines already collected during routine care at eight Italian hospitals, in fully anonymized form. No new tests or treatments are performed and patients are not contacted. AI models will be developed and tested on these data and compared with the contours used for treatment and with a subset drawn independently by several expert radiation oncologists on the same images in one/more institutes. The results are intended to support quality assurance, professional training and standardization of breast radiotherapy within the Italian National Health Service, including the development of a web-based educational platform for breast radiotherapy contouring.

title: DiabetIA: A Longitudinal Electronic Health Record Dataset for Diabetes Research from Mexico
desc: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) from primary care are scarce in low- and middle-income countries, and few have been made available to researchers in Latin America. We present DiabetIA, a longitudinal dataset derived from the primary care records of the Mexican Institute of Social Security (IMSS). The first release comprises 136,674 adults followed in six IMSS family medicine units in the state of Michoacan between 2005 and 2020, with more than 3.2 million visits summarized in 414,770 two-year windows with at least one visit. Each window includes demographics, ICD-10 diagnoses, anthropometry, vital signs, laboratory results and prescriptions, and type 2 diabetes diagnoses in the following year as prediction targets. At baseline, 24.4% of the patients had type 2 diabetes, 37.1% hypertension and 32.3% obesity. Technical validation assessed completeness, plausibility, consistency, temporal coverage and agreement with a state health survey. DiabetIA is freely available for download to support research on chronic disease trajectories and prediction in an underrepresented population.

title: VS-Suite: Automated Consensus Virtual Screening Platform for Improved Screening of Small Molecules
desc: Growing the recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine leaning (AI&ML) approaches accelerated small molecules screening against targeted proteins with limited computational resources and time. Finding accurate binding pose and affinity prediction is challenges task and traditional docking tools and lacks the reproducibility. Development of the Co-folding model is paradigm shift in drug discovery and development, allowing to predict protein ligand complexes without experimental crystal structures. Notably Boltz-2 predicts the complex structure along with binding affinity directly using protein FASTA sequence and ligand SMILES. Our previous studies confirmed that Boltz-2 is classify binder non-binders effectively. Autodock Vina and GNINA are widely used docking with knowledge and CNN based scoring functions allows to screen potential small molecules. We developed in-house VS-suite (Virtual Screening Suite) multi-environment conda orchestration designed to automate the docking workflow only using FASTA and SMILES string as inputs via streamlit-based browser GUI which integrates the boltz-2 for the complex structure prediction followed docking using AutoDock Vina for Gnina. Validation on 58 antiviral nucleoside analogues screened against SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro). VS-Suite is available at https://github.com/Vsubuchem-lab/Virtual-screening-suite-VS-Suite. This consensus approaches helpful in rapid screening of small molecules against selected targets. The findings and VS-suite support its utility as a rapid and reliable tool for hit identification and rational drug development.

title: Sports agnostic whole body sweat rate prediction using consumer-grade wearables and biophysics-guided machine learning
desc: This manuscript describes a novel consumer-grade wearable approach, leveraging a self-supervised learning architecture for sports agnostic (basketball, running, soccer, and tennis) activity intensity features, that integrates with a heat balance approach to predict whole-body sweating rate. We collected whole-body sweating rates and analyzed data from 234 trials from 147 volunteers. Wet-bulb globe temperature ranged from 11 to 35 ^oC. Wearable triaxial accelerometry and chest-strap heart rate data were processed through a pretrained neural network to predict metabolic components for heat balance equations. For the independent validation set, the mean absolute error for predicted whole-body sweating rate was 0.08 L/h for basketball, 0.17 L/h for soccer, 0.00 L/h for tennis, 0.03 L/h for running with 0.03 L/h for all sports combined. The accounted-for variance ( R ^2) for the whole-body sweating rate predictions were 0.76 for basketball, 0.73 for soccer, 0.82 for tennis, 0.94 for running and 0.79 for all sports combined. This study produced the following novel advancements: (1) first integration of wearable-derived activity features with a heat balance equation for sweat prediction; (2) first validated sport-agnostic wearable sweat prediction approach; and (3) first wearable method enabling a priori hydration management planning for exercise-heat stress conditions.

title: Large language model (LLM) & counseling for fetal malformations.
source: PubMed · Seminars in fetal & neonatal medicine
desc: [Seminars in fetal & neonatal medicine] Congenital anomalies affect approximately 3 to 5% of all pregnancies and represent a leading cause of infant morbidity and mortality worldwide. When a fetal malformation is detected on mid-trimester anatomic ultrasound, the clinical encounter that follows is not merely a medical consultation. It is an ethically charged event requiring the clinician to simultaneously respect maternal autonomy, apply beneficence-based clinical judgment, and, after viability, fulfill obligations to the fetal patient as well. This article applies the professional responsibility model, grounded in the ethics of medicine as a profession developed by John Gregory and Thomas Percival, to the counseling process following prenatal detection of a fetal anomaly. The model requires physicians to maintain scientific and clinical competence, to place the health-related interests of both patients as their primary concern, and to preserve medicine as a public trust. Within this framework, autonomy, beneficence, and justice each impose specific obligations, and a preventive ethics approach demands that clinicians anticipate and address ethical conflict before it escalates. Large language models (LLMs) offer genuine capabilities to support these ethical obligations: personalizing diagnostic information, bridging language and health literacy barriers, and extending clinical support beyond the encounter itself. However, LLM-generated content should be clinician-reviewed before reaching patients, informed consent processes should disclose AI involvement, and implementation should actively address equity across care settings. The physician's role as guide, interpreter, and compassionate presence cannot be delegated to any algorithmic system. With appropriate governance, LLMs amplify the art of counseling rather than replace it.

Bietti, IRCCS; conditions: Glaucoma; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 1200; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] The GlaukomAIcare study aims to evaluate an artificial intelligence (AI)-based system designed to help identify glaucoma, an eye disease that can damage the optic nerve and cause irreversible vision loss. The study will assess how accurately GlaukomAI identifies glaucoma compared with a diagnosis established by three glaucoma specialists using eye examinations, retinal photographs, optical coherence tomography (OCT), and visual field tests. The study consists of two phases. The first phase will compare patients with glaucoma and healthy participants to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the AI system. The second phase will assess whether the system can help ophthalmologists who are not glaucoma specialists identify patients who should be referred for specialist evaluation. Participants will undergo ophthalmological examinations and imaging assessments. All examinations will be completed during one visit or, if necessary, two consecutive visits within one week. The results may help determine whether AI-based technology can support earlier glaucoma detection and improve referral decisions in ophthalmological practice.

title: LifeLine.ai: A SigLIP-MedGemma Multimodal Framework with KTO Alignment for Open-Vocabulary 12-Lead ECG Report Generation
desc: Automated twelve-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation has historically relied on discriminative classifiers limited to closed-set diagnostic labels, signal reconstruction, or saliency heatmaps. While categorizing predefined arrhythmias well, these static classifiers cannot generate narrative clinical reports, incorporate patient history, or support interactive clinical question-answering (Q&A). We present LifeLine.ai, an end-toend multimodal Vision-ECG-Language framework for automated cardiac diagnosis and clinical reporting. After early attempts at waveform peak-tracking and coordinate mapping failed against complex morphological variations, we leveraged large-scale PhysioNet repositories (MIMIC-IV and PTB-XL). Because hardware limits precluded training on over 800,000 raw records, we curated a balanced subset to estimate performance, converting one-dimensional signals into 3x4 twelve-lead grids with continuous Lead II rhythm strips at the bottom. Our pipeline integrates YOLOv11s localization, a LoRAadapted Google SigLIP encoder, a trainable Multi-Layer Perceptron projector, and a 4-bit quantized MedGemma-4B model, complemented by a separate Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) pipeline built on collected user feedback and a multi-LLM consensus engine. On this compact subset, SigLIP outperformed Swin Transformer encodings (~0.21 vs. ~0.25 validation loss), achieving 71.0% open-vocabulary precision and a 75.0% contextual F1 score across a cloud deployment spanning Vercel, mobile apps, Amazon EC2, Firebase, Hugging Face, Modal GPUs, and lifelinecg-sdk. Our code is available at https://github.com/Asad939asad/ LifeLine.ai-.

title: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
desc: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei. To address this challenge, we propose CellTouch, a deep learning method for anisotropic 3D nuclei instance segmentation that predicts flow fields and a contact channel, which separates touching nuclei directly from the network output. Ablations showed that the contact channel is the key design element, and CellTouch outperformed state-of-the-art methods on in-house data and widely used public datasets. Most importantly, dense Z-sampling is not required: CellTouch segmented nuclei as accurately at a 2 um Z-step as at 0.5 um, reducing acquisition time and data volume four-fold.

title: Safety and accuracy diverge across deployment conditions in clinical large language models
desc: Clinical large language models (LLMs) are commonly scaled by increasing model size, context length, retrieval complexity, or inference-time compute, on the assumption that higher accuracy implies safer behavior. In medicine, where a few confident or evidence-contradicting errors can outweigh average performance, this assumption may be incomplete. We introduce Safety-Focused Evaluation of Scaling (SaFE-Scale) and instantiate it on RadSaFE-200, a 200-question text-based radiology multiple-choice benchmark with clinician-defined clean evidence, conflict evidence, and option-level labels for high-risk error, unsafe answer, and evidence contradiction. Thirty-four local LLMs were evaluated across six deployment conditions spanning closed-book, evidence-grounded, standard and agentic retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and max-context prompting. Clean clinician-written evidence, used as an upper-bound, produced the strongest joint gain, raising mean accuracy from 73.5% to 94.1% and reducing high-risk error from 12.0% to 2.6% and dangerous overconfidence from 8.0% to 1.6%. Standard and agentic RAG, max-context prompting, and inference-time compute improved selected metrics but did not reproduce this safety profile. Clinically consequential errors concentrated in a small subset of questions, and variance decomposition placed deployment condition above model family on every safety metric. Within this evaluation, clinical LLM safety did not track accuracy scaling but emerged as a deployment-level property.

title: Zero-code deep learning platform for diagnosing tuberculosis and COVID-19 via chest X-ray findings.
source: PubMed · The Libyan journal of medicine
desc: [The Libyan journal of medicine] Thoracic infections are deemed extraordinary cases that need to be detected early to improve their corresponding management. Among these, tuberculosis (TB) and coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) are the most dangerous and highly transmissible infections. They overlapped during the COVID-19 outbreak. One of the major diagnostic tools is the chest X-ray (CXR), which is attainable in most of the healthcare centers worldwide. Artificial intelligence (AI) has facilitated and improved the prediction of these and other diseases in recent years. Hence, the present study aimed to deploy a deep learning approach to predict TB and COVID-19 in comparison with healthy controls via CXR images. Google's Inception v3 model was used as the embedder, reputable for its speed and accuracy in image classification. Orange data mining software was utilized for the implementation of a deep neural network for diagnostic purposes of 268 each for controls, TB, and COVID-19 cases, while extracting 100 cases from each class for further external validation. A total of 100 neurons for 200 iterations and adaptive momentum (Adam) were used as the solver. The area under the curve (AUC) scored 1, while the accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-statistic were 98%. Upon internal validation for 300 cases, the constructed model displayed a slight drop in performance, with the AUC and other metrics decreasing to 0.997 and 0.967, respectively. However, the AUC and accuracy dropped to 0.88 and 66% after external validation. These findings highlight its potential as a diagnostic support tool while emphasizing the need for broader external validation and improved generalizability before clinical implementation.

title: Reproducible variability: assessing human vs. AI discordance in attempting to reproduce the same observational study
desc: Objective: Previously, nine expert teams given a published study and identical code sets produced nine substantially different cohorts, prompting the conclusion that analytic code cannot be reliably generated from natural-language description. We tested whether an artificial intelligence (AI) agent, given that same description, reproduces a cohort definition more faithfully and consistently than those teams. Materials and Methods: Against a claims database of 35.9 million patients, we executed 27 independent reproductions of that published glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist cohort definition: the nine published human definitions re-implemented deterministically (Arm A); nine independent AI agent runs given the source paper as published (Arm B); and nine given a rewrite that removed its internal contradictions (Arm C). All arms received identical frozen code sets. Agreement with a reference cohort was quantified by the Jaccard index. Results: Agents in Arm B achieved a median Jaccard index of 0.450 versus 0.259 for the human definitions, median pairwise agreement of 0.492 versus 0.149, and a 5.06-fold versus 32.0-fold size spread. Agent variation resolved almost entirely onto two criteria reported differently in the source main text and supplement. In Arm C, median agreement and median pairwise agreement both reached 1.000. Discussion: Changing only the analyst strongly trended towards improvement in fidelity, with every agent run more self-consistent than every human team. Changing the specification resulted in exact fidelity and self-consistency. Irreproducibility arose from both specification quality and inter-analyst variation. Conclusion: AI agents were more consistent than human teams when translating published natural-language descriptions into code.

title: L++: A Language for Programming Life
desc: Living systems run on a code written in DNA or RNA, but expressing that code as a model that scientists can write, run and read remains difficult. We present L++, a holistic programming language in which life can be described, simulated and, beyond that, designed; its nouns are biological, and people and AI systems can both write it. Molecules, reactions, compartments, cells, organs and populations are written directly and nest by containment, so one grammar spans a reaction and the population around it. Quantities carry units, objects take places in space, and values can be set in time. Named kinetic parameters select one family of rate laws, from mass action to cooperative enzyme kinetics, and a few operators write complexes, states and gene products in one line. Modules compose by import, and a process can be written by its inputs, outputs and rate before its mechanism is known; the aim is that one description can model an organism or design one. lppc compiles a program and lpps runs it, and a run repeats exactly with the same build, options and seed. Ten programs written with an AI assistant, from an enzyme in a tube to a lake ecosystem and a drug therapy from molecule to patient, show the language across levels of biological organization, and a genome-scale virtual Escherichia coli, reported separately, shows it holds a whole organism. Our ultimate goal is the Human Code: the human, from molecules to the whole body, written in L++ as a mechanistic model that runs.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven precision diagnosis and management of cutaneous lupus erythematosus: from lesion recognition and multi-omics profiling to clinical decision support.
desc: [Frontiers in medicine] Cutaneous lupus erythematosus (CLE) poses challenges in differential diagnosis, subtype classification, and longitudinal management because of its heterogeneous phenotypes and variable association with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This narrative review evaluates artificial intelligence (AI) evidence by clinical task, data modality, disease relevance, and validation maturity. Direct CLE studies provide early evidence for image-based lesion and subtype classification, including a multicentre multimodal system that improved dermatologists' diagnostic accuracy. A separate proof-of-concept study used natural language processing (NLP) to estimate Cutaneous Lupus Erythematosus Disease Area and Severity Index (CLASI) activity and damage scores from physical-examination notes. This text-based result should not be interpreted as automated severity scoring from clinical photographs: image-based lesion segmentation and CLASI estimation remain proposed applications. CLE transcriptomic, single-cell, and spatial studies reveal subtype-related B-cell signatures, interferon-associated keratinocyte states, specialized fibroblasts, and altered cell-cell communication; these findings are biological foundations for future models rather than validated patient-level prediction systems. Across applications, the level of CLE relevance is distinct from the maturity of validation. Current limitations include small or incompletely characterized disease-specific subsets, inconsistent image acquisition, uncertain independence of test cohorts, and limited prospective assessment of clinical utility. Progress requires transparent reporting of CLE-specific denominators, patient-level data separation, independent external validation, calibration, pigmentation-aware subgroup assessment, and clinician-supervised prospective evaluation. AI should therefore be regarded as an investigational decision-support approach for CLE, with clinical benefit established through disease-specific testing.

title: Non-Invasive Hemodynamic Assessment in Cardiogenic Shock
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: A.O.U. Città della Salute e della Scienza; conditions: Cardiogenic Shock; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 250; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Pulmonary artery catheter (PAC) monitoring is the reference standard for hemodynamic assessment in cardiogenic shock (CS), but it is invasive, resource-demanding and not universally available. HD-ASSESS-CS is a prospective, observational, multicenter study that will enroll consecutive adult patients with CS or pre-shock in whom PAC monitoring is clinically indicated. In each patient, a standardized comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography will be performed in close temporal proximity to invasive measurements, at baseline and at repeated time points during hospitalization. The study will assess the agreement between echocardiographic and invasive hemodynamic parameters, develop novel multiparametric echocardiographic indices (strain, Doppler and cardiac time intervals), and explore artificial intelligence models for automated estimation of hemodynamics from echocardiographic images. PAC placement is not performed for research purposes and AI outputs are not used for patient care.

title: How many large language models does title-abstract screening need? Theory, two replications and an evaluation at real prevalence
desc: Background and Objectives: Researchers increasingly combine large language models (LLMs) to screen titles and abstracts, assuming that more models make screening safer. We estimated how many models a screening ensemble needs, given correlated errors, and tested the answer on independent reviews and at real prevalence. Methods: We modelled correlated votes with a beta-binomial model and estimated, by bootstrap, the smallest ensemble capturing 95% of the net-benefit gain attainable over the best single model, accounting for human reading time and machine cost. Eleven LLMs from four developers voted blind on records from 13 SYNERGY reviews (derivation). We tested predictions fixed in advance on 10 and 16 Cochrane reviews from a public screening benchmark (replications) and evaluated a two-voter pipeline with an adjudicator on 11 complete benchmark collections and six reviews published in 2026. Results: Errors on relevant records were correlated (intraclass correlation 0.56 among eight different models; 0.75-0.78 among roles or copies of one model): eight models carried the information of about 1.6 independent ones. In derivation, the best single model, pair and trio reached sensitivities of 0.920, 0.975 and 0.981. Three or fewer models captured 95% of the attainable gain in at least 86%, 88% and 80.8% of bootstrap replicates of every scenario in the derivation set and the two replications, respectively. Six of seven registered predictions held in replication 1 and three of five sealed predictions in replication 2, where a fourth model added 2.1 percentage points to trios on average but 0.3 to the best trio. At real prevalence, the pipeline sent 94 of 96 included studies to human reading in the benchmark collections and 163 of 178 in the 2026 reviews (12.1% of 12,196 records sent to reading); its more sensitive voter alone sent 259 of 274 with 12.0%, at under a quarter of the machine cost. Conclusion: Because LLM errors are correlated, our results suggest two or three well-chosen models may suffice, but this needs deeper exploration in future studies. Which models are combined and how matter as much as how many, and any ensemble should be compared with its best single member.

title: FunDLM: A Foundation DNA Language Model for Fungi
desc: Background: Fungi are important pathogens and biotechnology resources, but lack a broadly applicable fungal DNA language model. Models trained on diverse fungal genomes can support functional interpretation of genomic variants and a broad range of genomic tasks. Results: We introduce FunDLM, a family of four DNA language models pre-trained on 426 fungal reference assemblies spanning 217 genera and 14.3 Gb of sequence. Without task-specific training, FunDLM-Medium-1024bp distinguished phenotype-associated missense variants of Saccharomyces cerevisiae from synonymous controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.875. It performed comparably to Evo 2, a generalist model with about 15 times more parameters, and better than Nucleotide Transformer v3. The model also recognized mutations that disrupt start codons or introduce premature stop codons in S. cerevisiae and the blast fungus Pyricularia oryzae. Its scores for missense variants, computed from DNA alone, correlated with those of protein language models in S. cerevisiae and two Fusarium species (Pearson correlation 0.57-0.75). After fine-tuning, FunDLM-Small-1024bp identified supernumerary chromosome sequences in four Pyricularia isolates not used for training (average precision 0.884), and FunDLM-Medium-1024bp recognized centromeres on a chromosome withheld from training (AUROC 0.908). Fine-tuned models also predicted three histone modifications in an isolate and on chromosomes not used for training (AUROC 0.910-0.996). Conclusions: FunDLM provides reusable sequence representations for assessing functional impacts of fungal variants as well as annotation of genomic and epigenomic features. The released models, data, code, and benchmarks support applications across fungal species.

title: Research hotspots and trends in machine learning for predicting postoperative outcomes of genitourinary cancers: A visualization analysis based on knowledge graphs.
source: PubMed · Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
desc: [Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine] Background Machine learning has been increasingly applied to predicting postoperative outcomes in genitourinary cancers. However, a comprehensive understanding of the research landscape, major hotspots, and emerging trends in this field remains limited.ObjectiveTo analyse the research status, hotspots and future trends of machine learning in predicting postoperative outcomes of genitourinary cancers.MethodsEnglish-language studies published up to 30 May 2026 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Annual publication trends were analysed using Excel, and VOSviewer and CiteSpace were used to visualise authors, countries, institutions, co-cited references and keywords.ResultsA total of 296 publications were included. Annual publication output showed an overall upward trend from 2021 to 2025, with a marked increase in 2025. China and the United States were the leading contributors, followed by England and Italy. The University of Texas System, Sun Yat-sen University, and the University of California System were among the most productive institutions. Co-citation analysis identified an interdisciplinary knowledge base encompassing cancer epidemiology, clinical guidelines, prognostic risk assessment, radiomics, and artificial intelligence. Keyword analyses highlighted machine learning, prostate cancer, deep learning, prognosis, and survival prediction as prominent research themes, with increasing attention to model evaluation, survival outcomes, and treatment planning.ConclusionThe bibliometric findings suggest increasing research attention to multimodal data integration, external validation, and clinical translation. However, further prospective studies are needed to establish whether these developments translate into meaningful improvements in clinical decision-making and patient outcomes.

title: Extracting generator-specific information from irregular brain field potentials: a comparative study of feature-based and deep learning approaches.
desc: Brain field potentials (FPs) reflect the combined activity of multiple neural sources, challenging the accuracy of their temporal series and their spatial origin difficult to establish from waveform inspection alone. However, FP generators obtained by independent component analysis exhibit characteristic temporal patterns and unique spatial profiles that allow their identification, even during apparently irregular activity. Here, we compared feature-based machine learning (ML) and end-to-end deep learning (DL) approaches to assess how effectively this information can be extracted from short segments and whether learning directly from raw signals offers advantages over predefined signal descriptors. We analyzed irregular FP-generator activity from multiple hippocampal generators in a dataset pooled across experimenters, recording devices, and electrode types. Feature-based approaches used predefined spectral and nonlinear descriptors to construct multidimensional representations, which were classified using seven ML algorithms: bagged decision trees (BAG), light gradient boosting machine (LGBM), quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA), random forest (RF), support vector machines (SVM), extreme gradient boosting (XGB) and multilayer perceptron (MLP). In parallel, convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and transformer architectures learned discriminative representations directly from raw signals. Performance was evaluated using animal-independent data partitions to assess generalization to previously unseen animals. Both approaches discriminated among FP generators from short segments of irregular activity. Raw-signal models generally achieved higher classification performance than feature-based approaches, although the latter also captured substantial generator-specific information. This suggests that discriminative information extends beyond the predefined descriptors and includes temporal patterns that can be exploited through direct signal learning. Classification across animals further supports the reproducibility of generator-related information despite variability in experimental conditions and recording procedures. These findings provide a scalable quantitative approach to identifying FP generators from irregular activity, opening new possibilities for investigating electrophysiological signals across physiological and pathological conditions.

Artificial intelligence as a precision diagnostic tool in gastrointestinal pathology.
desc: [Histopathology] Personalized medicine is on the rise, leading to increasingly granular treatment options. Consequently, pathologists are required to provide more detailed diagnoses to fully use the potential of these novel therapies. The number and complexity of grading systems and biomarker scoring methods are increasing. At the same time, the resulting rise in workload coincides with a growing shortage of pathologists, highlighting the need for new methods to ensure high-quality patient care in the future. This review explores the feasibility and readiness of artificial intelligence (AI) applications to alleviate routine diagnostic tasks in gastrointestinal (GI) pathology. It provides an organ-by-organ overview of both non-neoplastic and neoplastic diseases, with an emphasis on tools that show promise for direct or near-term clinical implementation. We found that numerous studies have investigated a wide range of diagnostic challenges, many of which have yielded encouraging results. While most tools remain in the research phase and often lack multicentre validation, commercially available AI solutions already exist for certain applications, in some cases even with regulatory approval for routine diagnostic use. In conclusion, most AI applications in GI pathology are still at a relatively early stage, and several challenges remain to be addressed. Nevertheless, many studies report promising results and suggest substantial advances in the near future. These developments have the potential to benefit both pathologists and patients by significantly expanding diagnostic capabilities while improving accuracy and reproducibility.

title: Development and Clinical Evaluation of Multimodal AI for Gastroscopy and Automated Report Generation
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Shandong University; conditions: AI (Artificial Intelligence), Endoscopy of Stomach (Procedure); type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 371000; status: RECRUITING] This mixed-methods study will include retrospective model development, cross-sectional validation, and prospective clinical validation. The study will generally follow relevant guidelines for AI-based clinical research. 1. Retrospective Model Development Approximately 300,000 gastroscopy examinations from our center will be retrospectively included. Available endoscopic data and related clinical information will be collected for model development and internal validation. Several publicly available gastrointestinal endoscopy datasets will also be included to increase data diversity. These datasets will provide supplementary data for model development and evaluation. The model will broadly support common gastroscopy-related tasks, such as lesion assessment, examination quality evaluation, and report generation. General data cleaning, quality control, and expert review will be conducted when necessary. 2. Cross-sectional Validation Approximately 70,000 gastroscopy examinations from a different time period will be consecutively included for independent validation. The model results will be compared with reference results established according to generally accepted clinical practice. Diagnostic standards will broadly follow relevant clinical guidelines and expert judgment. The purpose of this phase is to assess the model's overall diagnostic performance, report quality, generalizability, and stability using commonly accepted evaluation methods. 3. Prospective Clinical Validation A prospective clinical validation study involving approximately 1,000 patients will be conducted at our center. The model will be integrated into routine clinical practice to provide general assistance to physicians. Its outputs will be used for reference and will not replace physicians' final clinical decisions or signed reports. The study will generally compare clinical workflows with and without AI assistance. It will assess the model's potential effects on work efficiency, workload, clinical usability, and safety under real-world conditions.

title: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
desc: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions. In TEM-1, ESM2 accuracy fell with distance (Stiffler assay: {rho} = 0.72 below 8 [A] and 0.42 beyond 20 [A]), while the stability score rose ({rho} = 0.41 to 0.70). Adding stability to a model of ESM2, solvent accessibility and neighbour count improved cross-validated {rho} by 0.02 below 8 [A] and 0.10 beyond 20 [A], and the combined model did not decline with distance. The pattern held across binning schemes, in a continuous-distance model, and when any one of five contiguous distal stretches was removed. Two TEM-1 assays are nearly duplicates, and the Deng assay was too noisy to be informative. VIM-2 has only seven positions beyond 20 [A] and showed no detectable trend within 20 [A], so it neither supports nor contradicts the TEM-1 pattern. Nine distal TEM-1 positions remained more sensitive than the models predicted. In TEM-1, predicted stability was more informative than the language model far from the catalytic site, and the language model was stronger near it. Distance-stratified reporting could add to variant-effect benchmarks. The study is exploratory and uses one structure and one phenotype per assay.

title: Caries risk assessment support using artificial intelligence assisted panoramic radiography analysis.
desc: [Clinical oral investigations] Although artificial intelligence has shown promise in detecting dental pathologies on radiographs, integrating these findings into patient-level disease profiles and caries risk stratification remains challenging. This study aimed to address this gap by combining automated radiographic analysis with fuzzy logic. YOLOv11 based models were trained to automatically detect teeth and pathological findings (caries, restorations, missing teeth) in panoramic radiographs. The DMFT (Decayed, Missing, Filled Teeth) score calculated from the detections and a single anamnesis question regarding the patient's previous treatment history were incorporated into a Mamdani-type fuzzy inference system to generate a quantitative risk score and corresponding risk category (low, medium, or high). The developed model was evaluated using clinical panoramic radiographs from 200 patients. The YOLOv11l model achieved a recall of 0.936 in pathology detection. The resulting classifications showed agreement rates of 92.5% and 92.0% with the American Dental Association (ADA) and Caries Management by Risk Assessment (CAMBRA) protocols, respectively. Cohen's kappa values exceeded 0.87. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating radiographic detections and patient information into a structured patient-level assessment. The combination of automated image analysis and fuzzy logic provides a clinical decision-support framework for caries risk stratification based on panoramic radiographs. This approach offers an alternative way to integrate radiographic findings into a structured risk assessment process. The proposed system integrates automated radiographic analysis and risk stratification into routine dental assessment without requiring additional procedures. It can support clinical decision-making and facilitate communication with patients regarding oral health.

title: Artificial Intelligence Automated Telephone Consultations for Week 1 Post Surgery Cataract Surgery Patients
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Ufonia; conditions: Cataract Surgery, Cataract After Surgery, Cataract Patients, Cataract and Intraocular Lens (IOL) Surgery; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 100; status: RECRUITING] This clinical trial evaluates the safety, effectiveness, and acceptability of Dora, an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven conversational assistant, for conducting automated telephone consultations with patients one week after cataract surgery. Dora contacts patients by telephone to conduct a standardized post-operative assessment, identifying potential complications and concerns. The study enrolls patients in two phases: Phase 1 includes English-speaking participants and Phase 2 includes Spanish-speaking participants. The primary goal is to determine whether AI-automated telephone follow-up can safely and effectively identify post-operative issues requiring clinical attention while being acceptable to patients and clinicians.

title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
desc: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets. In an unpaired COVID-19 cohort, inferred responses were associated with severity, and IL-6 response scores correlated with plasma IL-6 concentrations. These findings support the use of biologically defined references to adapt pretrained representations for functional response inference.

title: Artificial intelligence-assisted semi-automated personal health data curation and reuse for myocardial infarction.
source: PubMed · European heart journal. Digital health
desc: [European heart journal. Digital health] Digital applications have high potential in myocardial infarction management. This study aims to harmonize personal health data using a workflow driven by an Artificial Intelligence-assisted virtual assistant prototype, then reuse the data to facilitate the creation of standardized patient summaries and risk assessment. The required configurations for data documentation and curation were developed to drive the workflow execution. With consent and data transfer agreements, data of patients with myocardial infarction were extracted from multi-source medical records, structured, and ingested into the workflow. After transformation, personal health data were mapped into concrete clinical concepts connected with specific relationships defined by the reference ontology, forming source health knowledge graphs as the basic structure of personal health knowledge graphs. Then the constructed graphs were validated using Shapes Constraint Language-based constraints, triggering the human-in-the-loop process to enhance data quality. Information queries were conducted for data reuse. Thirty eight out of 45 planned patients were recruited with signed informed consent. Thirty patients finalized the study. The overall successful data ingestion rate is approximately 83%. The average data quality score is 95.45/100. Constructed personal health knowledge graphs can be reused to represent medical information as an international patient summary and evaluate individual risk of future cardiovascular events by calculating the Second Manifestations of Arterial Disease risk score. Our proposed workflow is feasible for semi-automated personal health data curation and secondary use. It provides a potential solution to enhance medical data interoperability, thereby facilitating risk assessment in cardiovascular diseases.

title: Multicenter Clinical Validation of OSIS for Automated Ovarian Follicle Monitoring
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Fertoolity S.L.; conditions: Ovarian Follicle Monitoring, Controlled Ovarian Stimulation; type: OBSERVATIONAL; enrollment: 66; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Monitoring ovarian follicles is an important part of fertility treatments, as it helps healthcare professionals assess how the ovaries respond to stimulation. Traditionally, follicles are measured manually using two-dimensional (2D) ultrasound, a process that can be time-consuming and may vary between operators. This study aims to evaluate the accuracy of OSIS (Online System for Image Segmentation), an artificial intelligence (AI)-based software that automatically identifies and measures ovarian follicles using three-dimensional (3D) ultrasound images. Women undergoing controlled ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization (IVF), egg donation, or fertility preservation will participate in the study at fertility clinics in the United States and Europe. During their ovarian stimulation monitoring visits, conventional manual 2D ultrasound measurements will be compared with automated measurements obtained using OSIS. The study will also assess the consistency of measurements across different healthcare professionals, clinical settings, and ultrasound equipment, as well as the time required for each measurement method.

title: GeneArbiter improves plant genome annotations while preserving established gene models
desc: As plant genome resources expand, updating established annotations requires incorporating improved gene models without disrupting correct structures or stable identifiers. We developed GeneArbiter, an evidence guided framework that treats annotation updating as a correction preservation problem. GeneArbiter uses the current annotation as a backbone, integrates alternative models with RNA splice junction and homologous protein evidence, and applies constrained language model arbitration followed by deterministic release and identifier reconciliation. In rice MH63, GeneArbiter recovered 4,701 reference loci missed by the current annotation while losing 1,890 current exact loci, yielding a net gain of 2,811 exact matches and increasing the gene level exact hit rate from 70.77% to 77.77%. It retained 97.54% of protein coding genes in the mature TAIR12 annotation and improved protein set quality metrics across 16 plant genomes. Independent transcript and protein evidence further supported GeneArbiter selected structural revisions at reference discordant loci. These results establish GeneArbiter as a conservative and traceable framework for maintaining plant genome annotations as new predictions and biological evidence accumulate.

title: AI-integrated versus Standard Mammography Screening Pathways: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Diagnostic Accuracy.
desc: [Radiology. Imaging cancer] Purpose To compare the diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated and standard mammography screening pathways for breast cancer detection using Bayesian network meta-analysis. Materials and Methods This prospectively registered review searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through March 20, 2026, for diagnostic accuracy studies comparing two or more human-only or AI-integrated screening pathways using digital mammography or tomosynthesis. Bayesian bivariate random-effects network meta-analyses were fitted to a primary four-node and a secondary six-node network; risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 3 (QUADAS-3) and QUADAS-C tools, and certainty was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach. Results Thirty-eight studies, with more than 4.2 million examinations, were included. In the primary digital mammography network (15 studies), AI as an independent reader (sensitivity, 78.9%; specificity, 95.8%) performed similarly to double human reading (sensitivity, 77.7%; specificity, 96.2%). In the secondary network, AI reader assistance had the highest sensitivity (86.8%) and AI triage had the highest specificity (96.4%). Per 10 000 screened (prevalence, 0.8%), AI reader assistance detected nine more cancers than single human reading (69 vs 60), with 77 additional false-positive recalls (558 vs 481); AI triage had 27% fewer false-positive recalls than single human reading (353 vs 481), with the same cancer detection as double human reading (64 vs 64). Stand-alone AI had the lowest specificity (93.0%) and the most false-positive recalls (n = 694). Rankings are hypothesis-generating: Top-ranked pathways had overlapping credible intervals. Conclusion In this synthesis, AI reader assistance was associated with the highest cancer detection and AI triage with the lowest false-positive recall; stand-alone AI was not supported as a primary screening strategy in settings with existing radiologist capacity. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Breast Cancer Screening, Diagnostic Test Accuracy, Deep Learning, Digital Mammography, Mammography, Network Meta-Analysis, Screening Pathway, Computer-aided Diagnosis Systematic review registration no.
